en.question: Which MCP primitive is best suited to exposing the contents of a configuration file as background context, rather than as an action?

options.text: A tool, since the file must be fetched before its contents can be used.
options.note: A tool implies an invocable action with side effects or computation.

options.text: A prompt, since the configuration shapes how the model should behave.
options.note: Prompts are user-invoked templates rather than data exposure.

options.text: A hook, since configuration should be injected at a defined lifecycle point.
options.note: Hooks are a Claude Code lifecycle mechanism, not an MCP primitive.

options.text: A resource, identified by a URI and read by the application for context.

en.explanation: Resources represent data the host application can read and place into context. They are application-controlled and URI-identified, which suits reference material such as a configuration file.
